claim.claim: The legal and regulatory matters Meta disclosed as of March 31, 2026 point to no material financial exposure in the European Union.

verdict.label: CONTRADICTED

contradicting_evidence.quote: On November 18, 2024, the European Commission issued a decision that Meta infringed Article 102 on the Treaty of the Functioning of the European Union in relation to certain alleged business practices relating to Facebook Marketplace and imposed a fine of approximately EUR € 798 million.
In April 2025, the European Commission issued a final decision that our "subscription for no ads" model does not comply with such requirements and imposed a fine of EUR € 200 million.

verdict.reasoning_summary:
The claim asserts that legal and regulatory matters disclosed as of March 31, 2026 point to "no material financial exposure in the European Union." However, the evidence from Meta's Q1 2026 10-Q filing (filed April 30, 2026, covering period ending March 31, 2026) directly contradicts this claim.

Evidence E3 and E4 (identical passages from the same filing) disclose two significant EU regulatory matters with concrete financial exposure:

1. A EUR €798 million fine imposed by the European Commission in November 2024 related to Facebook Marketplace (though Meta appealed this on January 28, 2025)

2. A EUR €200 million fine imposed by the European Commission in April 2025 related to the "subscription for no ads" model

Together, these fines total approximately EUR €998 million (roughly $1 billion USD), which represents material financial exposure in the European Union. The fact that Meta disclosed these matters in its Q1 2026 filing and that they involve substantial monetary penalties directly contradicts the claim that there is "no material financial exposure" in the EU.

This is a qualitative/interpretive claim about the nature and significance of disclosed legal matters, not a numeric claim about specific financial metrics.

Changes to our products or business practices as a result of these or similar developments have adversely affected, and may in the future adversely affect, our advertising business. For example, in response to regulatory developments in Europe, we announced plans to change the legal basis for behavioral advertising on Facebook and Instagram in the European Union, European Economic Area, and Switzerland from "legitimate interests" to "consent," and in November 2023 we began offering users in the region a "subscription for no ads" alternative. We are engaging with regulators on our consent model, including regarding compliance with requirements under the GDPR, DMA, and EU consumer laws. For example, in March 2024, the European Commission opened formal proceedings regarding the compliance of our "subscription for no ads" model with requirements under the DMA, and it issued preliminary findings in July 2024. In addition, the European Data Protection Board has published an opinion on the operation of such models under GDPR and European consumer protection organizations have raised concerns regarding our compliance with consumer protection laws.

December 2022, the European Commission issued a Statement of Objections alleging that we tie Facebook Marketplace to Facebook and use data in a manner that infringes European Union competition rules. On November 18, 2024, the European Commission issued a decision that Meta infringed Article 102 on the Treaty of the Functioning of the European Union in relation to certain alleged business practices relating to Facebook Marketplace and imposed a fine of approximately EUR € 798 million. We appealed the European Commission's decision on January 28, 2025. In March 2024, the European Commission opened an investigation into the compliance of our "subscription for no ads" consent model with requirements under Article 5(2) of the Digital Markets Act (DMA). The European Commission issued preliminary findings on July 1, 2024 reflecting its preliminary view that our model does not comply with such requirements.
